lecture_title: Maxwell's Equations, Covariance, and Electromagnetic Waves

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_01.png
assets.rationale: Stanford title card with no mathematical or diagrammatic content.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: This program is brought to you by Stanford University.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: Shows the Lorentz force and the lecture's schematic pivot to tensor notation; the complete contraction is supplied in typeset form.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It's an anti-symmetric field tensor, which is built up out of the electric and magnetic fields.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: The electric and magnetic entries of the antisymmetric field tensor are complete and unobstructed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It transforms under Lorentz transformations as an anti-symmetric tensor.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: Clearly shows the one-dimensional scalar wave equation used to motivate the field-wave derivation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The wave equation is an equation with second derivatives.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: Shows the completed transverse electric and magnetic wave sketch at the actual point of the wave discussion.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: And they're also perpendicular to the motion of the wave.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: All four vacuum Maxwell equations are legible and minimally obstructed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: These are the basic Maxwell's equations, but these are the Maxwell's equations when there are no charges around.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: The dual tensor's visible entries verify the corrected electric-magnetic replacement rule.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: These are two tensor quantities, both of which have the same transformation properties.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: Preserves the explicit component check that reconstructs divergence and curl from the tensor equation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: That, my friends, is just del dot E equals zero.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: Shows the spatial second derivatives of E_x at the conclusion of the double-curl calculation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: You'll see that this is just a wave equation for the component E_x.
assets.caption_hint: Wave equation for the electric field

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_10.png
assets.rationale: The oriented area element and d-sigma dot J flux factor are both visible.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: That means the current is perpendicular to d sigma. Then this product is zero.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_11.png
assets.rationale: Shows the integral relation between changing charge density and current divergence after Gauss's theorem.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: It says that the derivative with respect to time of the charge density, plus...

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_12.png
assets.rationale: The local continuity equation is complete, centered, and unobstructed.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: If it's to be true in every frame of reference, it better have the form of some invariant equation.

assets.name: lecture_58_figure_13.png
assets.rationale: Shows the sourced Maxwell equations beside the covariant equation partial_mu F^{mu nu}=J^nu.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: And so this equation would be invariant and the same in every reference frame, assuming that J transforms as a vector.
assets.caption_hint: Sourced Maxwell equations in covariant form
